newsitem.title: GERMANY: EMU effect on Buba jobs seen modest initially - paper.
newsitem.headline: EMU effect on Buba jobs seen modest initially - paper.

text.p: The 16,000 employees of Germany's Bundesbank have little reason to fear over jobs at the launch of Europe's currency union in 1999, Bundesbank council member Dieter Haferkamp was quoted as saying on Friday.
"The effects of European economic and monetary union (EMU) on jobs will initially be modest," Haferkamp said in the Bundesbank's in-house magazine, quoted in Germany's Sueddeutsche Zeitung newspaper.

The council member said current discussions showed national central banks would remain operational in many areas within the framework of the future European Central Bank (ECB), which will be based in Frankfurt.
But Haferkamp said the Euro would have on effect on levels of qualifications among employees -- with more focus needed on language ability, specialised knowledge and presentation skills.
The European Monetary Institute (EMI), the forerunner of the ECB, currently employs 64 Germans, of which 41 are Bundesbank employees on sabbatical, in a total staff of 240, the paper said.
The ECB is scheduled to come into being in 1998.
